fidelity_modes.faithful: Preserve source chapter order and most source content. Improve hierarchy, rhythm and interaction without materially restructuring the argument.
fidelity_modes.adaptive: Preserve all material claims and evidence while allowing consolidation, reordering and compression to improve the narrative. Default mode.
fidelity_modes.restructured: Rebuild the narrative around the document's core question and evidence rather than its original section order. Must record every structural transformation and retain all important source claims.

chapter_header.purpose: Fast access to major chapters and visible current chapter.
chapter_header.desktop: sticky horizontal navigation or compact menu

reading_progress.purpose: Show overall progress without distracting from content.

micro_navigation.purpose: Move between chapters and significant scenes without losing orientation.
micro_navigation.desktop: right-side rail with chapter markers, nested scene dots, active label, previous/next controls
micro_navigation.mobile: compact previous/next controls plus current chapter label
micro_navigation.behavior: scroll to semantic scene anchors, not arbitrary viewport offsets

rules: Use emphasis to encode hierarchy or argument, not decoration.
Prefer one strong highlighted phrase over multiple competing highlights.
Scroll highlighting is suitable for progressive argument, definitions and key conclusions.
Never encode essential meaning only through colour or animation.

none.use: Default when motion adds no explanatory value.

crossfade.use: Transition between related images, states or time periods.

wipe_left.use: Reveal a next state or compare layers with a directional reading.

wipe_right.use: Reveal a previous/alternate state or directional comparison.

wipe_up.use: Progress upward through stages, layers or chronology.

wipe_down.use: Reveal a descending sequence or remove a layer.

parallax.use: Add depth to contextual photography or chapter transitions.

fixed_background.use: Hold context while narrative text progresses.

zoom_in.use: Move from overview to detail; maps, images, diagrams, evidence.

zoom_out.use: Move from detail to system view or conclusion.

pan.use: Travel across a large map, image, timeline or diagram.

blur_to_focus.use: Shift attention to a key claim or selected element.

grayscale_to_color.use: Signal activation, selection or before/after state when semantically justified.

color_to_grayscale.use: Signal deactivation, loss or backgrounding when semantically justified.

scale_reveal.use: Introduce a quantified result, object or focal visual.

draw_path.use: Show routes, dependencies, sequences, processes or trajectories.

progressive_build.use: Build a chart, matrix, roadmap, process or evidence chain in reading order.

flipbook.use: Animate a meaningful sequence of states or explain a mechanism. Avoid decorative use.

horizontal_track.use: Present ordered phases or a bounded sequence that benefits from spatial progression.

sticky_step_change.use: Keep a visual context fixed while explanatory steps change.

rules: Use strong source or contextual visual.
Keep copy short.
Background video must be muted, looping and have a still fallback.
Use when reading is more important than motion.
Do not force every paragraph into an interactive scene.
One key idea only.
Allow visual breathing room before or after high-density scenes.
Use overlay/gradient for legibility.
Do not place dense body copy over busy media.
Frames must represent comparable states or a meaningful sequence.
Prefer hard change for frame-by-frame animation and crossfade/wipe for distinct states.
The visual must change because the explanation changes.
Avoid excessive frame counts without explanatory benefit.
Provide distinct mobile crops or alternates.
Keep text column position compatible with media focal points.
Use when overview-to-detail context matters.
Each point needs a semantic reason for movement.
Choose chart type from analytical question, not aesthetics.
Animate annotations or data states only when sequence helps understanding.
Always expose source and units.
Only for truly decision-relevant numbers.
Never manufacture a headline metric by unsafe aggregation.
Use temporal order only when time is the real organising dimension.
Use actual source schedule data.
Do not infer dates or durations not present in the source.
Axes and point positions must be sourced or explicitly labelled qualitative transformation.
Use common dimensions and consistent scales.
Use for a small bounded set of parallel items.
Do not hide important hierarchy behind equal-sized tiles if items are not equal.
Arrows must mean something explicit: sequence, dependency or causality.
Do not infer relationships absent from the source.
Use a simpler stakeholder list if relationship evidence is weak.
Only use geography when spatial location contributes to the argument.
Do not geocode uncertain entities without marking uncertainty.
Avoid near-duplicate images.
Use captions when images carry evidence.
Foreground video may include sound and controls; background video should not be the only carrier of important information.
Prefer charts for pattern recognition and tables for exact lookup.
Quotes must be traceable to the exact source wording.
Keep available but visually secondary to the main narrative.
Do not introduce new unsupported conclusions.
Use only when standard primitives cannot express the semantic requirement.
Must be responsive, accessible and tested.

selection_rules.when: two or more values whose relationship matters
large image contains multiple meaningful areas
ordered items should be discovered progressively
source contains a strong chart or diagram
source has a coherent visual identity

reuse_same_image.exception: deliberate callback or comparison with explicit semantic purpose

media_policy.source_image_preference: prefer relevant source visuals before adding stock/contextual imagery
media_policy.external_image_rule: external imagery may establish context or mood but must not imply a source fact not present in the document

motion_policy.low: safe default; subtle fades, depth and focus shifts
motion_policy.medium: use when movement explains sequence, comparison, hierarchy or navigation
motion_policy.high: rare; only for mechanisms or frame-by-frame explanations
motion_policy.reduced_motion: replace transforms and frame animation with static final states or short crossfades

rules: Infer the source document's visual identity before planning the story: dominant palette, accent colours, typography character, logo/brand motifs, chart colours, image style and whitespace density.
When the source has a coherent brand system, preserve its recognisable visual identity while adapting layout to scrollytelling.
Do not replace a coherent source palette with StoryScro default colours unless the user explicitly requests rebranding.
Reuse strong source charts, diagrams and images when they carry evidence; crop or animate them rather than redrawing without need.
External contextual imagery may add atmosphere or spatial context but must not be presented as source evidence and must not imply a documented event that is not shown in the source.
If the source is visually weak or inconsistent, keep any meaningful brand cues but allow the renderer to regularise spacing, typography and hierarchy.

phases: ARRIVE: establish the scene and let the reader understand the frame before anything changes.
SETTLE: hold the title/thesis long enough to make the scene legible.
REVEAL: introduce one meaningful state or item at a time unless overview-first is analytically necessary.
HOLD: keep each state stable long enough to read; avoid continuous motion for content that needs comprehension.
EXIT: transition cleanly to the next scene without leaving overlapping copy behind.
rules: Do not show all future steps and then repeat them one by one unless the overview itself is an explicit analytical message.
For sequential evidence, start with a neutral or empty frame, then reveal the first item after the intro hold.
When several items share a frame, non-active items should normally be hidden or visually demoted while the active item is being explained.
Titles and changing step copy must occupy collision-safe zones; if they cannot coexist, compact or fade the title before step copy appears.
A scroll event should usually produce one intelligible change, not several simultaneous changes.
Prefer discrete state changes with short transitions over constant movement when the reader needs to inspect data or text.

hover: Use hover to reveal secondary explanation, focus a chart element, expose a tooltip or preview a detail.
Hover must never be required to understand essential content because touch devices do not have hover.
click: Use click/tap for optional drill-down, source detail, lightbox expansion or a temporary focus state.
The reader must be able to return to the narrative without losing scroll position.
